newsitem.title: FINLAND: Cyclicals help sluggish Helsinki end shade higher.
newsitem.headline: Cyclicals help sluggish Helsinki end shade higher.

text.p: * Shares end modestly higher as cyclicals generate active interest despite weaker dollar. Rauma shines. Operators to focus on forestry companies' earnings reports next week. * HEX +0.15 pct at 3,006.65, adv-decl 32-34, 32 unch * Volume 398.32 million markka, 34 pct in Nokia * .HEF1 +0.49 pct, .HEB1 -1.52 pct, .HEM1 +0.51 pct ------------------------ (May 7) -----------------------------

Ignoring a weaker dollar, Finnish cyclical stocks with engineering group Rauma and forest industry companies in the lead pulled the Helsinki bourse to a marginally higher close oin Friday, brokers said.
But trade was quiet as many operators extended the Ascension Thursday holiday into a long weekend, they said.
Rauma rose 5.5 percent in lively demand following its main owner UPM-Kymmene's decision earlier this week to cut its stake in it through an offering of shares, brokers said.
Forestries outperformed, boosted by big overnight gains in U.S. paper stocks and in anticipation of their Q1 reports.

"There is a lot of demand for UPM-Kymmene, and it seems to be mostly from the U.S.," one broker said. "We will be focussing on forest industry results next week and there will be some key figures from the U.S. as well," another broker said.
Metsa-Serla is due to release first-quarter earnings on Monday and UPM-Kymmene's Q1 report is due out on Thursday.
Banks underperformed and Merita extended Wednesday's losses after reporting a sharp rise in Q1 earnings, mainly based, however, on gains from a downsizing of its equity portfolio.
Nokia closed 3.00 markka lower at 325.00 markka, accounting for a good third of total turnover.
